title: NANSEN module
description: module.nansen.json at the root of a module folder: a versioned bundle of fragments, methods and file adapters. Everything a module provides is listed here by path, relative to the module folder; nothing is found by scanning. A project uses a module by listing it in its modules.

addons.description: Toolboxes and packages the module's methods use, which the add-on manager (addons.list, addons.install) lists and installs.

dashboard.description: Scripts the dashboard runs when a project uses the module: each adds pages with N.registerPage. Files of the module they need are read with modules.resource.

presets.description: Option presets (nansen.options documents) of the module's or other modules' methods. A project's own preset of the same name is used instead.

source.description: Where it comes from: one of github, pip or conda

github.description: owner/repository: the default branch is downloaded into the add-ons folder

pip.description: A pip requirement, installed into the running Python

conda.description: A conda-forge package: not installed by NANSEN, which says how to

check.description: A function (MATLAB) or module (Python) that is there once the add-on is installed

pathOrder.description: MATLAB: where the add-on goes on the path; end keeps it behind NANSEN's own functions

setup.description: MATLAB: a script in the add-on, run in its own folder after it is downloaded (to compile, for example)
